meta.method: Monthly series -> subtract each month's long-term average (removes the seasonal cycle) -> annual mean of anomalies -> Theil-Sen slope with 95% confidence interval + Mann-Kendall significance test (OLS regression as a cross-check).
how_to_read: Slope per decade: how fast the variable changes (Theil-Sen estimate).
95% confidence interval: plausible range for the slope; if it excludes zero the trend is likely real.
p < 0.05 (Mann-Kendall): the trend is 'statistically significant'. Not significant does not mean no change - a longer record may be needed.
Seasonality is removed first, so summer-vs-winter swings do not hide the long-term trend.
limitations: Only 26 annual values; autocorrelation is not corrected.
Zones are simple averages of 0.5 x 0.625 degree grid cells (63 cells); zone tests are not corrected for multiple testing.
NDVI is available only as one region-wide average (no zones). Relative changes are unreliable when the baseline is near zero.
Climate variables are MERRA-2 model-based estimates, not station measurements.

temp_c.name: Air temperature
temp_c.definition: Air temperature about 2 metres above the ground. Rising values mean warming.

precip_mm_day.name: Precipitation
precip_mm_day.definition: Average rain and snow, in millimetres of water per day.

humidity_g_kg.name: Specific humidity
humidity_g_kg.definition: Grams of water vapour in each kilogram of air at 2 metres. Warmer air can hold more water vapour.

ndvi.name: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
ndvi.source: MODIS Terra MOD13Q1 (250 m, 16-day composites, averaged monthly)
ndvi.definition: How green the land looks from space. Near 0 means bare ground or desert; higher values mean more or healthier plants.

examples.title: Is the region getting warmer?
examples.takeaway: Average air temperature rose about 0.48 °C per decade (95% CI 0.34 to 0.61), roughly 1.2 °C between 2000 and 2025 (p < 0.001): significant.

examples.title: Same region, opposite rainfall trends
examples.takeaway: In the North-West zone rainfall fell by 0.12 mm/day per decade (p = 0.022), while in the South-West zone it rose by 0.08 mm/day per decade (p = 0.008) (that area is very dry, averaging only 0.23 mm/day, so the absolute change is small). The whole-region average shows no significant trend (p = 0.692), hiding both.

examples.title: Is the vegetation getting greener?
examples.takeaway: The region-wide NDVI rose about 0.0042 per decade (3.0% of its average), p < 0.001. Most of the area is desert, so values are low. There is no matching regional rainfall trend (p = 0.692), and irrigation or land-use change are not in our data, so we cannot say what drives it.
